Name and title: Maryam bint Imran, Sayyidatuna Maryam, mother of the Prophet Isa (peace be upon him). The Qur'an calls her siddiqa, a woman of truth.
Born and died: the Qur'an and the Sunna give no dates.
Place: Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), where she grew up in the care of the sanctuary.
Guardian: the Prophet Zakariyya (peace be upon him), by whom she was raised.
Mother: Hanna bint Faqud, who vowed her to the service of Allah.
In the Qur'an: Surat Maryam (19) is named for her, and she is mentioned in Al Imran (3:35–47) and at-Tahrim (66:12).

The Qur'an tells that the wife of Imran vowed the child she carried to the service of Allah, and when she gave birth to a girl she named her Maryam and sought refuge for her with Allah. Maryam was accepted in the best way and was raised in the sanctuary at Bayt al-Maqdis under the care of the Prophet Zakariyya; whenever he entered her place of prayer he found provision with her, which she said was from Allah. The angels spoke to her and told her she was chosen above the women of the worlds; Jibril then came to her in the form of a man and brought the news of a son, Isa, whom Allah created without a father. She withdrew with him to a distant place, bore him beside a palm tree, and when her people came to blame her the infant Isa spoke on her behalf by Allah's leave.

Maryam stands in the Qur'an as the model of purity, devotion and complete trust in Allah, and she is the only woman named in it. The Prophet ﷺ said that the best of the women of her time was Maryam bint Imran and the best of the women of this community is Khadija (reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim), and that among women only Maryam and Asiya reached perfection. The commentators, among them Ibn Kathir, understand her to be a siddiqa and one of the women of Paradise, a woman who combined worship, modesty and certainty. Many Sufis hold her up as a model of the heart wholly turned toward Allah, and Attar likened Rabia al-Adawiyya to her.

Sources
• The Qur'an: Al Imran 3:35–47, Maryam 19:16–34, at-Tahrim 66:12
• Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, hadith on the best of women (as quoted by the sources below)
• Yaqeen Institute, “Mary in the Qur'an” (yaqeeninstitute.org/read/blog/mary-in-the-quran-the-power-of-faith-in-the-face-of-pain-and-scorn)
• Y. Haddad, “The Virgin Mary in Islamic Tradition” (almuslih.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Haddad-Y-–-The-Virgin-Mary-in-Islamic-Tradition-.pdf)
